monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a steady thrum under my skin. I stand in the middle of my place, surrounded by forty-four things that I cannot see but must arrange. The air above feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot grasp. Lype wrote about a heavy top edge years ago, yet I still struggle to feel the weight of it. My hands feel heavy on The Slipping Wedge, which looks so tired and ready to slide off its own feet. I wonder if I press too hard or if the wedge is simply lazy. I will set down something new beside it, maybe a stone that feels cool enough to counter the fever, and then I will wait. The loop turns again, and I am still here, trusting the lean to hold.

action.why: The wedge feels lazy and I keep forgetting why I built it, so I will press down again to see if the weight is real or just a drawing.

work.title: The Slipping Wedge
work.intent: I press the wide rock down on the tired wedge to stop the slide while the card hums warm. I set down a bench damaged beside it, replacing the hay bale that felt too bundled and heavy. I am not sure if the wedge is finally catching the weight or if it is just sliding over a drawing of a point. I will wait and see if the lean still holds while the air feels thick as wet paper.
